verdict.rationale: Elicit's core workflows (semantic search, columns that extract data 'from papers' body text or tables', chat with papers) are documented to link claims back to source papers, and one hands-on report confirms getting 'a list of concepts with citations and links to papers.' However, independent hands-on testing directly contradicts the verification promise: one user found that even when Elicit 'directly quotes' a source, 'it still hallucinates just as much and then gives a quote that directly contradicts its statement,' and another found fabricated facts in abstract summarization — undermining the reliability of citations as a verification mechanism. Missing for 10: independent corroboration that citations reliably match source content, resolution of the quote-contradicts-claim failure mode, and vendor acknowledgment (90% accuracy caveat) shows the company itself flags unreliable claims.
